disposition_reason: Per-sample XRF concentrations of As, Pb, Hg and Cd (plus Ca, Fe, K, Zn) in 30 market geophagic white clays from Kumasi are printed.

study.design: market survey of geophagic clay with health risk assessment
study.origin: not stated (white clay in Ghana is typically sourced from Anfoega, Volta Region, per the introduction)
study.market: 10 markets in the Kumasi Metropolis, Ashanti Region, Ghana
study.method: Portable XRF (Thermo Niton XL3t) on dried, crushed, 250 µm-sieved clay per USEPA Method 6200; six samples also by ICP-MS after modified aqua regia digestion (results figure-only)
study.qa: XRF calibrated with reference material SAR-M (USGS 180-673); replicate analysis for precision; bioaccessibility QA used procedure blank and laboratory control sample

findings.integrity_flag: Mean (0.81 mg/kg) is below the stated XRF LOD (1.70 ppm) and equals the Table 1b total (24.18) divided by 30, i.e. non-detects counted as zero.
findings.notes: Only 3 of 30 samples had detectable mercury.

regulatory_or_exposure.value: As 3.0, Pb 3.0, Hg 0.6, Cd 0.3 µg/kg bw/day

unresolved: Table 2b gives amounts of arsenic and lead in 70 g of clay (derived intake, labelled ppm), not concentrations; not recorded.
ICP-MS arsenic results for six samples are figure-only (Fig. 3); the text says ASA3 and AYI1 disagreed between methods.
Zinc bioaccessibility (Table 6) is a percentage, not a concentration; not recorded.
XRF is a screening technique with ppm-level LODs; cadmium non-detects are bounded only at 1.9 mg/kg.
